text:
matt: ok team — quick sync. I'm prototyping a small-surface approach for internal APIs: typed protobuf/gRPC between services, but keep a tiny http/json "edge shim" for external callers and web clients. thoughts on quotas, header propagation, and rollout UX?
asha: i like typed internal contracts. question: how do we pass tenant identity + quota claims from the edge shim to backend services without serializing large JWTs every hop?
tomas: we can propagate a short signed claim blob — 3 fields: tenant_id, route_claims, usage_bucket. keep it compact and base64. backend verifies with short-lived key from control plane.
kevin: that reduces header bloat. but it adds a verification call surface — maybe verify lazily in services and only call control plane when claim is stale.
sara: telemetry concern: if shim is translating proto->json, we lose native latency/size telemetry unless we correlate with an id. please add a request-id header that persists across translations (eg x-rw-request-id).
matt: agreed. plan: shim sets x-rw-request-id and x-rw-route-shard (for routing weights). services must include them in traces and metrics. that gives us token-level cost attribution and per-route histograms.
asha: quotas — should enforcement live at the edge shim or be baked into services? edge prevents over-subscription, but services should do best-effort checks for safety. double-checks are cheap if we use cached counters.
tomas: enforcement split: primary at edge (strict), secondary at service (soft limit + circuit). service will return 429 with a structured body that contains fallback hints.
kevin: rollout UX: want canary routing by header, not by deployment only. propose a control-plane API: set route_claim weight for matcher -> edge applies x-rw-route-shard = variant when forwarding. no redeploys.
sara: this helps A/B tests and gradual rollouts. also think about realtime console: we need a per-route latency/err rate panel and a lightweight signal for degraded quality (embedding/regression).
infra-bot: deploy check: canary header propagation tests failing in staging (shim->service trace mismatch).
matt: noted. action items: 1) implement x-rw-request-id and x-rw-route-shard in shim (+ docs). 2) prototype compact claim blob format + verification caching in service SDK. 3) add service-side soft quota with 429 structured response. 4) console: per-route histogram and canary weight UI mock.
asha: small sample for claim header: ```
X-RW-Claims: v1.b64(tenant:acme;rb:prod-read;u:bucket42).sig
```
tomas: and verification pseudocode: ```
claims = decode_b64(header)
if now - claims.ts > cache_ttl: verify_with_control_plane()
else: accept
```
kevin: edge-case: browser clients may not send custom headers (CORS). shim should accept an auth cookie and produce headers server-side. also consider JSON-only clients using long polling / SSE — streaming gRPC semantics won't map one-to-one.
sara: telemetry for streaming: mark stream open/close events and report partial token counts every N seconds. console can surface active-stream counts.
matt: ok this is solid. decision for now: internal gRPC+proto, HTTP shim at edge that injects compact claim + request id + route shard, enforcement split edge/service. we'll iterate on exact claim encoding and verification caching.
kevin: +1. i'll take the shim header/CORS changes.
asha: i'll draft the SDK verification cache.
tomas: i'll add trace instrumentation hooks and example dashboards.
sara: i'll sketch console panels and the canary-weight editor flow.
infra-bot: created task RH-789 for header propagation tests and RH-790 for claim format spec.
matt: thanks. follow up in #eng-platform next week with prototypes. :thumbsup:
